capability_findings.observed: TL-UL (TileLink Uncached Lightweight), the OpenTitan bus spec variant of TileLink. The spec states it follows the TileLink 1.7-draft document (1.7.1 referenced in the same README) with lowRISC user extensions, one request and one response per cycle and no burst transactions.

A channel: a_valid, a_opcode[2:0], a_param[2:0], a_size[TL_SZW-1:0], a_source[TL_AIW-1:0], a_address[TL_AW-1:0], a_mask[TL_DBW-1:0], a_data[TL_DW-1:0], a_user (tl_a_user_t) and d_ready. D channel: d_valid, d_opcode[2:0], d_param[2:0], d_size, d_source, d_sink[TL_DIW-1:0], d_data, d_user (tl_d_user_t), d_error and a_ready. This is the same struct pair used by the uart/gpio top ports.

TL_AW=32, TL_DW=32, TL_DBW=4, TL_SZW=clog2(clog2(TL_DBW)+1)=2, TL_AIW=8 (a_source/d_source), TL_DIW=1 (d_sink), TL_AUW=23 (a_user). These are the elaborated values; a_size therefore encodes 1/2/4-byte transfers and a_source is an 8-bit ID.

a_opcode legal set is PutFullData=3'h0, PutPartialData=3'h1, Get=3'h4 (no other opcodes). d_opcode is AccessAck=3'h0 for writes and AccessAckData=3'h1 for reads; the adapter returns AccessAckData for a Get regardless of error.

tl_a_user_t = {rsvd[RsvdWidth-1:0], instr_type (mubi4), cmd_intg[6:0], data_intg[6:0]} with RsvdWidth = TL_AUW-4-7-7 = 5 bits; TL_A_USER_DEFAULT sets instr_type=MuBi4False and both integrity fields to all ones. RACL role and CTN UID are carried in a_user.rsvd and extracted with top_racl_pkg::tlul_extract_racl_role_bits / tlul_extract_ctn_uid_bits. tl_d_user_t = {rsp_intg[6:0], data_intg[6:0]}.

The generated reg_top instantiates tlul_cmd_intg_chk directly on tl_i. That checker recomputes inv-64/57 SEC-DED over {a_address, a_opcode, a_mask, a_user.instr_type} and inv-39/32 over a_data, and pulses err_o = a_valid & (|err | |data_err). The reg_top latches it (err_q) and drives intg_err_o = err_q | intg_err | reg_we_err, where reg_we_err is a prim_reg_we_check one-hot check of the register write enables. intg_err_o is wired to alerts[0] (and to no other alert). NOTE: the reg_top's own tlul_adapter_reg keeps CmdIntgCheck=0 (default) and its intg_error_o port is left unconnected, so the integrity error does not travel through the adapter's internal checker; it comes from the separately instantiated checker.

reg_error = addrmiss | wr_err | intg_err is passed to the adapter as error_i; the adapter registers d_error = error_i | err_internal at a_ack and forces d_data to all ones for every write and for any errored read, so an errored read never returns register contents. err_internal = addr_align_err | tl_err | instr_error | intg_error where tl_err is the protocol checker (opcode not in the legal set, a_size>2, size/address misalignment, a_mask outside the addressed lanes, PutFullData mask not covering the size, invalid instr_type mubi, instruction-fetch write) and addr_align_err flags a write with a_address[1:0]!=0. addrmiss = (reg_re||reg_we) ? ~|addr_hit : 0; wr_err flags a sub-word write whose byte enables are not permitted by the per-register PERMIT mask. Reads of unmapped offsets inside the window return the default case value '1.

The reg_top generates both response integrity fields with tlul_rsp_intg_gen(EnableRspIntgGen=1, EnableDataIntgGen=1): rsp_intg is inv-64/57 SEC-DED over {d_opcode, d_size, d_error} and data_intg is inv-39/32 over d_data. The adapter's own data-integrity generator is disabled (EnableDataIntgGen(0)) and d_sink is tied to 0.

One prim_alert_sender per alert, instantiated with AsyncOn=AlertAsyncOn[i], SkewCycles=AlertSkewCycles and IsFatal=1'b1; alert_req_i is the register-integrity error (alerts[0]) and alert_test_i is driven from the ALERT_TEST register bits as (alert_test.q & alert_test.qe). alert_ack_o and alert_state_o are left unconnected. alert_tx_t = {alert_p, alert_n}; alert_rx_t = {ping_p, ping_n, ack_p, ack_n}. The sender implements a 4-phase differential handshake FSM (Idle -> AlertHsPhase1 -> AlertHsPhase2 -> Pause0 -> Pause1), asserting alert_p/n and waiting for the receiver's ack_level; IsFatal=1 latches the request until reset so the handshake is re-issued indefinitely.

NumAlerts=1 from the generated reg_pkg, so alert_tx_o and alert_rx_i are 1-element arrays and the generate loop creates exactly one sender. AlertAsyncOn defaults to all ones (asynchronous handshake, CDC-safe) and AlertSkewCycles to 1, matching top_pkg::AlertSkewCycles=1; these are the values used by the earlgrey top instance as well.

A single bussified prim_intr_hw with Width=NumIOs=32 and the default IntrT=Event drives all 32 interrupts: intr_gpio_o is a registered LEVEL output (intr_o <= status & INTR_ENABLE, FlopOutput=1) whose bits come from the 32-bit W1C INTR_STATE register, so an asserted bit stays high until software writes 1 to clear it. INTR_TEST can force any bit. The event for bit i is (rise & INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING[i]) | (fall & INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING[i]) | (level_high & INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH[i]) | (level_low & INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW[i]); rise/fall are derived from the filtered pin value registered one cycle earlier. Offsets: INTR_STATE 0x00, INTR_ENABLE 0x04, INTR_TEST 0x08, ALERT_TEST 0x0c, DATA_IN 0x10, DIRECT_OUT 0x14, MASKED_OUT_LOWER 0x18, MASKED_OUT_UPPER 0x1c, DIRECT_OE 0x20, MASKED_OE_LOWER 0x24, MASKED_OE_UPPER 0x28, INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING 0x2c, INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING 0x30, INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH 0x34, INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW 0x38, CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER 0x3c, HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID 0x40, HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN 0x44.

Inputs: each cio_gpio_i[i] is filtered by prim_filter_ctr (AsyncOn=GpioAsyncOn=1 -> 2-stage synchronizer, CntWidth=4, thresh=4'hF) enabled by CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER[i]; the filtered value data_in_d is written to the DATA_IN register unconditionally and one-cycle-registered to derive event_rise/event_fall. Outputs: cio_gpio_o = cio_gpio_q and cio_gpio_en_o = cio_gpio_en_q, both registered. cio_gpio_q is updated with priority DIRECT_OUT.qe > MASKED_OUT_UPPER.data.qe > MASKED_OUT_LOWER.data.qe, and a masked write only changes the enabled lanes: q <= (mask & data) | (~mask & q); MASKED_OUT_UPPER covers [NumIOs-1:16] (= [31:16] here) and MASKED_OUT_LOWER [15:0]. MASKED_OUT/ MASKED_OE .mask reads back as constant 0 (hw2reg mask.d = 0). The enable path is identical for DIRECT_OE / MASKED_OE_LOWER / MASKED_OE_UPPER. The IP has no tristate primitive: value and enable are separate digital ports for the pad wrapper.

With GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1 (module default, used in this closure) a strap_en_i pulse samples the filtered pin values once per reset cycle: HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN_VALID is set and HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN latched, and sampled_straps_o.valid/data mirror those registers. With GpioAsHwStrapsEn=0 the whole block is replaced by tie-offs (sampled_straps_o = 0, no register updates); the pinned earlgrey top instantiates gpio with GpioGpioAsHwStrapsEn=0, which was separately elaborated as a variant with the identical closure file set.

Same generated RACL structure as uart: with the recorded default EnableRacl=0, racl_addr_hit_read/write fall back to addr_hit, racl_error_o.valid is always 0 and no access is blocked. With EnableRacl=1 the role is extracted from a_user.rsvd, one-hot encoded, compared against the per-register RaclPolicySelVec-selected read_perm/write_perm, register writes are gated by racl_addr_hit_write, and a policy miss on a hit address raises racl_error_o.valid. Unlike uart, gpio's generated default for RaclErrorRsp is 1'b1, so the RACL error is folded into the adapter error_i (returning tl_o.d_error=1) as soon as RACL is enabled, even though EnableRacl itself is 0 in the recorded command.

BlockAw=7 gives a 128-byte register window (last register HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN at 0x44). tlul_adapter_reg is instantiated with RegAw=7 and addr_o = {a_address[6:2], 2'b00}: only bits [6:2] are decoded inside the IP and higher address bits are ignored, so no aliasing check exists inside the IP. Reads are returned word-aligned regardless of a_size.

Elaborated with the module defaults: AlertAsyncOn=1'b1, AlertSkewCycles=1, GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1, GpioAsyncOn=1, EnableRacl=1'b0, RaclErrorRsp=1'b1, RaclPolicySelVec='{NumRegs{1'b0}}. Reason: the module-declared defaults are elaborated as written; the pinned earlgrey integration overrides AlertAsyncOn (AsyncOn[4]) and sets GpioGpioAsyncOn=1 / GpioGpioAsHwStrapsEn=0, which was elaborated as a separate variant with the identical closure file set. NumIOs=32, NumAlerts=1, NumRegs=18, NumInpPeriodCounters=0 and BlockAw=7 come from the pinned generated gpio_reg_pkg.

unsupported.reason: sources.lock.json records the generator as regtool/topgen with status pending_input_closure_and_reproduction and tool_version null. regtool/topgen was not executed in this task; the checked-in generated files hw/top_earlgrey/ip_autogen/gpio/rtl/gpio_reg_pkg.sv and gpio_reg_top.sv are used and sha256-pinned, so the register map is verified against the pinned bytes but not reproduced from hw/top_earlgrey/ip_autogen/gpio/data/gpio.hjson.

Only prim_alert_sender is instantiated inside this closure; no prim_alert_receiver / alert_handler peer is included, so alert_ack_o and alert_state_o are unconnected and the 4-phase differential handshake cannot complete.

The recorded command elaborates the module defaults, where EnableRacl=0 makes racl_error_o.valid constant 0, so RACL enforces nothing even though RaclErrorRsp defaults to 1. The EnableRacl=1 configuration was separately elaborated (exit 0, identical closure file set, log runs/soc-source-elaboration/opentitan/gpio_racl_enabled.log) but no behaviour has been simulated.

The pinned earlgrey integration instantiates gpio with GpioGpioAsHwStrapsEn=0 (and GpioGpioAsyncOn=1); the recorded command uses the module defaults (GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1, GpioAsyncOn=1). The earlgrey configuration was separately elaborated (exit 0, identical closure file set, log runs/soc-source-elaboration/opentitan/gpio_earlgrey_params.log). Strap sampling (sampled_straps_o / HW_STRAPS_*) is therefore part of the recorded closure but disabled in the earlgrey configuration.

The gpio inout pad is split into digital cio_gpio_i / cio_gpio_o / cio_gpio_en_o ports and no pad/tristate primitive is part of the closure; the physical inout merge and pad attributes are outside it.
